Olivia — thanks again for the redlines this morning. Attached is our annotated MSA (redwood-msa-annotated.pdf) with inline comments on the IP/indemnity sections. Two discrete things we want to confirm so we can get your legal team a clean counter: 

1) Open-source / third-party dependency carve-out: your text suggests a broad carve-out for any third-party claim tied to OSS, even where Redwood ships a modified component. For us that’s a meaningful operational and risk difference. Can you confirm Acme's intent: is the requested exception limited to unmodified OSS or broader? We can propose explicit language that preserves the carve-out for unmodified permissively licensed code and narrows it elsewhere.

2) Notice & defense delegation: your redline requires Redwood to be notified of claims through the ordering/contact route but does not specify escalation steps for suspected IP claims (e.g., immediate security/legal intake, evidence checklist, parallel product mitigations). We usually propose a delegated-notice routing (customer -> ACME legal -> Redwood legal) plus a 72-hour acknowledgement SLA and an evidence checklist to speed triage.

I’ve copied Kimberly and Marissa from Legal/Product so they can weigh in on (a) acceptable carve-out text and (b) practical notice routing plus an evidence list template. If those two pieces are resolved we can move to defense-control wording and insurance thresholds.

Next steps I propose: you send the Acme redline on the IP/indemnity clause only (we saw a full redline but want the canonical clause) and we’ll return a narrow alternative. Target: get to a mutually acceptable clause for MSA + Order Form by next Thursday.

Thanks,

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the annotated draft. Apologies for the terse redline — our in-house team is trying to standardize language across several vendors. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Intent on OSS carve-out: Acme's position is to exclude from Redwood's indemnity any claim that rests solely on use of third-party open-source components where (i) Acme has independently chosen, installed, or modified the OSS component, and (ii) Acme has not requested Redwood to alter or maintain that component. We are not seeking a blanket exemption for modified OSS created by Redwood, but we want to avoid swapping back-and-forth by adding a short, operational definition.

- Defense/control: we would prefer Redwood to assume defense/control for third-party IP claims (subject to mutual cooperation) but we expect an explicit cap tied to the Order Form value and for Redwood to carry primary responsibility for settlement decisions involving monetary relief. If Redwood insists on declining defense, we will seek a mandatory assignment to external counsel with step-in rights.

- Evidence: we've attached the clause we typically use and an internal checklist; happy to accept your 72-hour acknowledgement SLA.

Team — quick legal take and proposed client-facing compromise below. Important to balance operational tractability with acceptable risk.

Legal analysis (short):
- OSS carve-out: we should accept a narrowly drafted carve-out limited to (i) OSS not forked/or modified by Redwood; (ii) OSS governed by standard permissive licenses (Apache, MIT, BSD). Avoid one-line broad "OSS" exclusions. We can require the Order Form to include a short checkbox and a description of any OSS components the customer claims to control. That makes triage easier and shifts burden on customer to disclose relevant components.

- Defense/control: we can accept to "defend and control" subject to the following constraints: 
  * Redwood has right to select counsel and manage the defense, subject to customer approval of counsel where customer reasonably objects.
  * Redwood will not enter into settlements that: (i) require admission of liability beyond remedial steps; (ii) require Redwood to grant any right to Customer in Redwood's intellectual property; or (iii) impose non-monetary performance obligations without customer consent.
  * Settlement monetary authority: Redwood can settle up to $150,000 without customer consent; settlements between $150,001 and $1,000,000 require customer written consent; settlements > $1,000,000 require executive escalation and are subject to the indemnity cap.

- Indemnity cap / escrow / insurance: recommend proposing an indemnity cap tied to Order Form value (e.g., 12 months of paid fees) with an escrow threshold for claims above $250,000 and a covenant to maintain commercial general liability/tech E&O with a $2M limit (or pursue per-deal insurance buy-ups).

Proposed clause language (for client-facing counter):
"Third-Party IP Claims. Redwood will, at its expense, defend Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Service as provided by Redwood infringes a third-party's intellectual property rights, provided Customer (a) gives prompt written notice of the claim, (b) provides Redwood reasonable cooperation and information necessary for the defense, and (c) grants Redwood sole authority to defend and settle the claim; provided, however, that Redwood will not enter into any settlement that (i) admits liability on behalf of Customer, (ii) requires Redwood to grant any right to Customer in Redwood's intellectual property, or (iii) imposes non-monetary obligations on Customer without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may settle claims involving monetary relief up to $150,000 without Customer consent. Settlements exceeding $150,000 require Customer's written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

OSS carve-out (operational):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood will have no obligation to indemnify or defend to the extent the claim arises solely from (i) Customer's use of third-party open-source software that Customer has modified or installed without Redwood's involvement, or (ii) third-party open-source components identified in the Order Form as Customer-controlled. Customer will identify any such components at order entry and update Redwood if changes are made to those components."

If we sign off on the $150k/$1M thresholds and the escrow/insurance proposal, I think this is defensible and will get Acme to the middle ground. Otherwise they are likely to push for unlimited defense authority and no cap.

Happy to refine.

Olivia / Damian — thanks for the clarity and for looping in counsel. Attached is our proposed compromise language (I pasted the key text below). High level: we will accept a limited OSS carve-out tied to customer-controlled components (to be disclosed on the Order Form) and we will assume defense/control for third-party IP claims with the settlement-authority/consent thresholds Kimberly recommended. We also propose an escrow threshold of $250,000 and to maintain Tech E&O insurance at a $2M limit; we can offer a per-deal buy-up if Acme needs a higher limit.

Key excerpt (for quick review):
"Redwood shall defend and indemnify Customer from third-party claims of IP infringement for the Service as delivered, provided Customer promptly notifies Redwood, cooperates with Redwood, and grants Redwood sole authority to manage the defense. Redwood may settle claims for monetary amounts up to $150,000 without Customer consent. For settlements between $150,001 and $1,000,000 Redwood will not settle without Customer's written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Claims above $1,000,000 will be escalated to executives for resolution and are subject to the indemnity cap set forth in the Order Form.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood shall have no indemnity obligation for claims arising solely from Customer-controlled or Customer-modified third-party open-source components identified in the Order Form. Customer will include a list or description of any such components at order entry.

In addition, for claims likely to exceed $250,000 the parties agree to trigger an escrow review and discussion of insurance buy-up options.

We are open to a specific agreed cap (12 months fees) or negotiating a dollar cap. Please let me know if Acme can live with these guardrails and we will incorporate the precise Order Form checkbox/field to make the carve-out operational.

If you'd like, we will also send a short runbook for the notice flow (72-hour acknowledgement SLA, evidence checklist items) to reduce time-to-remediation.

Best,
Karthik
